floor-field-01.png.notes: TIER B. Four independent draws of ONE prompt, assembled by the baker into a 2x2 mosaic: -01 top-left, -02 top-right, -03 bottom-left, -04 bottom-right. Crop 2304x2304 from each — an INTERIOR window, never touching the frame edge, which is where the model puts its vignette — reduce 4x (two box-halvings) to 576x576, assemble to 1152x1152 = WorldPxR at RS=4. QUANTIZE ONCE, AFTER ASSEMBLY: four independently median-cut quadrants carry four palettes and the joins appear as colour steps across the middle of the board. Equalize per-quadrant mean and stddev BEFORE quantization if the joins fail. Verification, both mechanical: (a) block flatness — split the assembled 1152x1152 into an 8x8 grid of 144px blocks, assert every block's mean luma is within +/-3 of the field mean (kills vignettes, which are what make a mosaic seam findable); (b) join test — mean |dLuma| across the x=576 column join and the y=576 row join must not exceed 1.25x the mean |dLuma| of interior columns/rows. Consumed by plateAt as `base` in place of BgDark; plateAt keeps its per-tile shade hash, its PanelPeriodPx joints, its flecks and pinholes, and gains the two §3.4 deltas missing today (+3% luminance inside the safe ring; amber-etched Fortress chamber floor). Sample point is the ABSOLUTE world pixel (wx,wy) — this is why the field is full-arena and non-tiling: no two of the 2,040 ground tiles may match.
floor-field-01.png.prompt:
Orthographic front view, straight on, no perspective, no camera tilt.
Single key light from the upper left. No cast shadow (the shadow is drawn separately).
Background: flat pure #00FF00, edge to edge. There must be no other green anywhere.
No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no signature.

MATERIAL SWATCH — this entry overrides the framing lines above. There is no subject, no background and no key colour in this image: the material fills the frame edge to edge, fully opaque, and there must be no green pixel anywhere. There is no key light and no shadow — the lighting is flat, even and shadowless, identical in every part of the frame, with no vignette, no falloff, no gradient, no hot spot and no visible light direction. This image is not composited onto the dark slate ground; it IS the dark slate ground.

Seen from directly overhead, perfectly flat on: the bare deck plate of a machine floor. Cold desaturated blue-grey engineered stone — cast mineral aggregate, quarried, poured and ground flat. Surface character at three scales and nothing else: a broad slow cloudiness about one twentieth of the frame across; an even fine granular tooth over the whole surface; and sparse isolated speckles — a few brighter mineral flecks and a few darker pinholes, scattered evenly and never clustered into a shape.

Nothing structural anywhere: no panel lines, no joints, no seams, no tiles, no grid, no bricks, no plates, no rivets, no bolts, no hatches, no drains, no scratches, no scuffs, no tracks, no footprints, no wear paths, no stains, no rust, no dirt, no moss, no vegetation, no water, no cracks, no edges, no border, no frame, and no object of any kind. The renderer draws the panel joints, the tile grid and every luminance step on top of this material; anything here that reads as a line will fight them.

Even coverage is the whole job: any square region of this frame must be interchangeable with any other. Mean tone RGB(40,48,57); every pixel inside the desaturated blue-grey range #1C242B to #4E5E6B, with the darkest and brightest points of the frame no more than one third of that range apart.

The subject will be composited onto a dark slate ground, RGB(40,48,57) — light it for that.

Palette, strictly:
  structure / stone / chassis  -> desaturated blue-grey, #1C242B to #4E5E6B only
  living signal / emission     -> pale cyan phosphor #A5E3EE, highlights to #EAF7FA
  matter, loot, money, energy  -> warm amber #FFB454
  contact shadow / ink line    -> near-black blue #10161C
Nothing warm except the amber. Nothing green. Nothing saturated red unless asked.

wall-face.png.notes: TIER B — the most dangerous asset in the plan (risk #4). Crop 1536x1536 as an INTERIOR window, reduce 4x to 384x384. Consumed ONLY by parapetColorAt's `else: base` branch: the 4-ray openDistDir edge classification stays verbatim, StoneInk contact line at edge<=1, lit/shadowed bevel to WallBevelPx=8, roof seam at (wx+wy) mod RoofSeamPeriod. Fortress reuses the SAME material at shade(+22) — a brighter ramp, not a second image (§3.4). SEAMLESSNESS IS THE BAKER'S JOB, NOT THE MODEL'S: no supported frame size is a 2^k multiple of 384 (1024/384=2.67, 2048/384=5.33, 4096/384=10.67), so the crop is always an interior window and whatever tileability the model produced is cut away. Baker: (1) measure — edgeDelta = mean|L(x=383,y) - L(x=0,y)| over y, and the same for the y axis; interiorDelta = mean|L(x,y) - L(x+1,y)| over the interior; require edgeDelta <= 1.25 * interiorDelta on both axes; (2) if it fails, apply a deterministic wrap-blend over a 32px band (1/12 of the tile) with a cosine window, then re-measure; (3) block flatness — 8x8 grid of 48px blocks, each mean luma within +/-3 of the image mean, which is what keeps the 16-tile repeat undetectable. Order matters: wrap-blend BEFORE median-cut, or the blend invents off-ramp colours that the palette lint then rejects.

Seen from directly overhead, perfectly flat on: the flat top surface of one monolithic block of dark blue-grey engineered stone — the roof face of a fortress parapet, the material inside the wall and nothing else. Dense fine granular grain, a faint broad cloudiness beneath it, and a light even scatter of small darker inclusions.

This is NOT masonry and must contain no drawn structure of any kind: no bricks, no courses, no block joints, no mortar lines, no seams, no bevels, no chamfers, no rims, no edges, no corners, no highlights, no shadows, no rivets, no bolts, no panel lines, no cracks, no chips, no wear, no lettering. The renderer derives every edge, bevel, roof seam and contact line from the collision mask and paints them over this material; one drawn edge here decouples the art from the geometry and the tile is rejected.

Seamless and tileable in both axes: this frame must repeat against itself with no visible join. Keep the character uniform and fine; keep the brightness identical at all four edges and in the middle; and put no feature, blotch, dark patch or bright patch larger than one sixteenth of the frame anywhere.

Darker and denser than a floor: mean tone near #36444F, every pixel inside #1C242B to #4E5E6B.

The subject will be composited onto a dark slate ground, RGB(40,48,57) — light it for that.
